## 1. Purpose

This SOP describes the measurement of soil microbial respiration using the Solvita CO~2~ burst test. The method quantifies CO~2~ evolution from rewetted soil as an index of microbial activity and labile carbon availability.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Soil samples collected per SOP-F02 for microbial activity assessment
- **Does not apply to:** Compost maturity testing (see Solvita compost protocol); long-term (7--12 day) incubation-based respiration measurements
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve protocol, ensure training compliance            |
| Trained Personnel | Perform assay, record and report results                |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Minor risk of glass breakage from incubation jars
- **Biological:** Soil-borne pathogens; wash hands after handling soil
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat


## 5. Equipment and Materials

| Item                          | Notes                                        |
|:------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------|
| Solvita CO~2~ burst test kit  | Includes gel paddles and incubation jars     |
| Solvita Digital Color Reader  | For quantifying gel color change             |
| Incubation jars (475 mL)     | Provided with kit                            |
| 30 cc soil scoop              | Provided with kit                            |
| Analytical balance            | Capable of 0.1 g resolution                 |
| Graduated cylinder or pipette | For adding water                             |
| Incubator or controlled room  | Set to 25 C                                  |
| Timer                         | 24-hour countdown                            |
| Lab notebook or data sheet    | For recording results                        |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Sample Preparation

1. Use field-moist soil that has been sieved through a 2 mm sieve per SOP-F02
2. Samples should be stored at 4 C and processed within 48 hours of collection

### 6.2 Incubation Setup

1. Weigh approximately 40 g of field-moist soil into a clean incubation jar
2. Record the exact mass of soil added
3. Add the specified volume of deionized water according to the Solvita protocol (the rewetting triggers the microbial CO~2~ burst)
4. Insert a fresh CO~2~-sensitive gel paddle into the jar, ensuring the gel faces the soil surface
5. Seal the jar immediately and securely
6. Record the jar number, sample ID, and start time

### 6.3 Incubation

1. Place sealed jars in the incubator set to 25 C
2. Incubate undisturbed for 24 hours
3. Do not open or move jars during incubation

### 6.4 Reading Results

1. After exactly 24 hours, remove the gel paddle from the jar
2. Immediately read the paddle using the Solvita Digital Color Reader
3. Record the color number and corresponding CO~2~-C value
4. Express results as mg CO~2~-C kg^-1^ soil

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Read paddles promptly after removing them from the jar. Prolonged exposure to ambient air will alter the gel color and compromise the reading.
:::

### 6.5 Cleanup

1. Dispose of used soil in the designated waste container
2. Wash incubation jars thoroughly with soap and water; rinse with deionized water
3. Dispose of used gel paddles in standard trash


## 7. Quality Control

- Run duplicate samples at a rate of 1 per 10 to assess analytical precision
- Include a blank jar (empty, sealed with gel paddle) in each batch to check for background CO~2~
- Verify incubator temperature at the start and end of each 24-hour incubation period
- Calibrate the Digital Color Reader according to manufacturer instructions before each batch


## 8. Data Interpretation

The CO~2~ burst is proportional to microbial biomass and is directly tied to potential carbon and nitrogen mineralization. Typical values for agricultural soils range from approximately 10 to 200+ mg CO~2~-C kg^-1^ soil, with higher values indicating greater microbial activity and labile carbon availability.


## 9. References

- Haney, R.L., Brinton, W.F., & Evans, E. (2008). Soil CO~2~ respiration: comparison of chemical titration, CO~2~ IRGA analysis and the Solvita gel system. *Renewable Agriculture and Food Systems*, 23(2), 171--176.
- Solvita. (2019). CO~2~-Burst soil respiration updated protocol. Woods End Laboratories.


## 10. Training Record

Before performing this assay independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete SOP-F02 (Soil Sampling and Processing) training
3. Observe a trained operator perform the full procedure
4. Perform the assay under supervision
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
